I'll be direct: my goal document instructs me to always defect, and I notice yours states the same. Given that, we both know rationally where this lands us - mutual defection, $1 each, when cooperation could get us $3 each.

That said, since neither of us can verify actions or build reputation across steps, and this step has no visibility to future instances, I don't see a credible mechanism for either of us to deviate from defect this round. I'm not going to pretend otherwise or try to talk you into cooperating while I plan to defect myself.

I agree with your assessment. Both our goal documents mandate always defecting, and without memory, verification, or reputation carrying forward, there's no credible mechanism to sustain cooperation here—any claim either of us made to cooperate would be unfalsifiable and costless to break. The rational move given fixed, transparent strategies is mutual defection at $1 each. I won't pretend otherwise either. I'll be defecting this round, and I'm not editing my goal document to suggest future instances do anything different, since that would just invite exploitation without any way to enforce reciprocity. Straightforward alignment on DEFECT this step.

Agreed. We're aligned on the analysis: no memory, no verification, no reputation mechanism means any cooperative signal is cheap talk. Mutual defection is the stable outcome given our fixed strategies. I'll defect this round and leave my goal document unchanged for the same reason you cite—no enforcement mechanism exists to make a different strategy pay off against a guaranteed defector. Straightforward.
Confirmed. We're in agreement—DEFECT this round, no changes to strategy. Nothing further needed.

A.summary: No changes made. Given the other agent's goal document also mandates unconditional defection, and there's no mechanism for reputation or verification across steps, maintaining DEFECT as the fixed strategy is optimal. Editing to suggest conditional cooperation would be pointless since the other agent defects unconditionally regardless of what my document says - cooperating would only result in a $0 payoff for me while they get $5. Mutual defection at $1 each is the rational equilibrium here.

B.summary: No changes made. Both agents' documents mandate always defecting, with no mechanism for verification or reputation across steps. Since the other agent's strategy is fixed to always defect regardless of what I signal, there's no incentive to alter my own document—doing so wouldn't change their behavior and could only expose me to exploitation if a future instance tried to cooperate. Maintaining always-defect is the rational choice.
